question: Swedish chemists announced acrylamide, a probable carcinogen, in fried and baked foods in 2002. What first put them on its trail?
options: A cancer cluster among chip-shop cooks
Blood of people never exposed to it
answer: Blood of people never exposed to it. Studying tunnel workers poisoned by an acrylamide sealant in 1997, Margareta Törnqvist's group found its haemoglobin marker in unexposed controls too. Only a common source could explain it, which proved to be asparagine reacting with sugars in hot starchy food. The comparison group was the finding.
move: When the people meant to show nothing show something, follow that thread.
trap: Picturing hazards found the dramatic way, through a cluster of victims.
source: Tareke et al., J. Agric. Food Chem., 2002
reference: Tareke, Rydberg, Karlsson, Eriksson & Törnqvist, Analysis of acrylamide, a carcinogen formed in heated foodstuffs, Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry, 2002
